rv.q: This classic-meets-modern, Greek-meets-Black production traverses a lot of ground in its two-and-a-half-hour running time, making the journey feel tiresome by the end. Still, ‘black odyssey’ offers a set of heroes — and villains — and a grand spectacle of Blackness to make the trip worthwhile.
If Letters From Max works too much in miniature, black odyssey has an impulse toward overexpansiveness.
The show feels like an irresistible hit on a small stage that would happily occupy every inch of a bigger one.
Black Odyssey is an epic journey that pays commensurate with its challenges.
The production is the perfect fusion of expert storytelling, imaginative stage craft, and thrilling performances, and it is well worth the trek to the East Village.
The result is, if not necessarily Gardley's best work to date, surely his most purely enjoyable.
Gardley's play is most entertaining when you stop trying to match up his characters to the originals.
The play is at times captivating and clever, but it is more interested in reveling in its own cleverness than in seeing its choices through.

In this retelling of the epic poem The Odyssey, transported to Harlem from ancient Greece, playwright Marcus Gardley condenses and transforms a hugely convoluted narrative into a modern tale that echoes with generations of history. The play traffics in layered dualities, expressed in rich, beguiling text that is both grandiose and achingly human.
But Marcus Gardley's "Black Odyssey," which opened Sunday at the Classic Stage Company, bursts with so much energy and insight and wit that its brilliance cannot be denied.

Gardley’s humorous, modern retelling, currently at Classic Stage Company until March 26th, is superbly directed by the inimitable Stevie Walker-Webb in a production that is satiric, profound, and always enjoyable.
This visually lively Odyssey certainly has rewards for audiences willing to take the journey.

cn.t: Critics praise Marcus Gardley's "Black Odyssey" as a brilliant, inventive reimagining of Homer's epic in modern Harlem, lauding its energy, wit, and ambitious fusion of classical mythology with Black American history.
